messages:
beth-support: heads up — customer ACME reported a big latency regression right after yesterday's runtime push. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~320ms, p99 from ~260ms -> ~820ms on text-gen workloads (gpt-small-ish). They've attached traces and a repro curl.

beth-support: repro info pasted below (customer gave us permission):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-open-ql-7b","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64,"batch_size":4,"seq_len":64}'
```

beth-support: they see the spike on hosted region us-west-2, only after the deploy that enabled new kernel selection heuristics (flash_attention + sdpa toggles). Logging: request id 0a1b2c3d -> see attached tail logs: `kernel_selector: picked flash_attn_v2 for model redwood/gpt-open-ql-7b, seq_len=64, batch=4` then long stall before first token.

devon-runtime: thanks — assigning. any sample traces/pprof? can you paste the full header from their logs (trace ids)?

beth-support: trace ids: trace=tr-98765, span=span-333. I pasted the clipped log above; full log in case: `2026-02-12T14:03:12Z INFO kernel_selector: model=redwood/gpt-open-ql-7b seq_len=64 batch=4 selected=flash_attn_v2 compile_flags=-DUSE_FLASHATTENTION`

maria-engr: interesting — flash_attn usually helps, but for short sequences and small batches the call overhead can dominate if kernel implementation expects larger seqs. also we had the new SDPA fallback path that accidentally increases synchronization for int8/quantized paths.

aj-ml: do we have perf regression tests that match this customer's profile (seq<=64, batch<=4)?

devon-runtime: yes, but our CI usually targets mixed seq>256 workloads. I just ran local bench to replicate. baseline (before toggle): p95=118ms p99=247ms. current (with kernel selector change, commit abcd1234): p95=321ms p99=835ms. logs show extra 300-400ms in kernel warmup/compile and an extra memcpy on path with sdpa enabled.

leo-compiler-bot: quick diff between kernels: flash_attn_v2 introduces a small per-invocation kernel-init sequence when compiled with -DUSE_FLASHATTENTION=1 that is amortized for longer sequences. sdpa_kernel has more branching for quantized attention that triggers on quant_mode=INT8.

kai-sre: can we toggle kernel selection per-request while we debug? any env var or runtime flag?

devon-runtime: yes — we have runtime override ENVs. temporary mitigation: set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINTS to avoid flash_attn_v2 for seq_len<=128. e.g.
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINTS="avoid:flash_attn_v2;prefer:sdpa_kernel:cond(seq_len>=256)"
```

maria-engr: another faster mitigation: enable the compile-time fast-path guard that bypasses flash init for small seqs. revertable flag in build: `-DFASTPATH_SMALL_SEQ` (we compiled it off in last deploy). I can trigger a partial rebuild and push a canary image.

beth-support: customer asked for an ETA — they want a short-term setting they can apply on their dedicated capacity, or we can toggle for their tenancy on hosted.

devon-runtime: for hosted we can flip a per-tenant kernel preference in routing config. I'll push a canary config that sets `kernel_policy=avoid:flash_attn_v2` for their tenant id. Rolling to 5% now.

aj-ml: long-term we should improve kernel_selector heuristics: use a cost model that accounts for seq_len, batch_size, quant_mode, and measured init overhead. I can add telemetry hooks to feed measured latency per kernel back into selector.

maria-engr: quick steps I'm taking:
- revert the compile option that disabled FASTPATH_SMALL_SEQ on canary image
- add runtime guard: if seq_len<128 prefer sdpa_kernel with low-overhead path
- add automatic fallback: if observed p95 for last 5m > baseline*1.5, auto-switch to fallback kernel for that route

devon-runtime: ops plan:
- canary rollback for tenant (apply avoid flash_attn_v2) at 14:40 UTC
- monitor p95/p99 for 15m windows -> if p99 drops, promote to 25% then 100%
- create incident ticket INC-4728 and notify support + account team

beth-support: customer on call at 15:00, please have a short changelog and rollback plan ready.

kai-sre: also adding temporary alert to detect reappearance: query: `sum(rate(latency_p99{route="/generate",tenant="acme"}[5m]))` > threshold. I'll set a PagerDuty override for this customer during the window.

leo-compiler-bot: reproduced locally with script — attaching quick repro script for engineers:
```
# repro.sh
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "$API/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-open-ql-7b","input":"hi","max_tokens":64,"batch_size":4}' >/dev/null; 
  sleep 0.2; 
done
```
Run with `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINTS="avoid:flash_attn_v2"` to compare.

maria-engr: FYI the root cause summary: kernel_selector change (commit abcd1234) introduced a heuristic bias to pick flash_attn_v2 aggressively; for small seqs on quantized models flash_attn_v2 has higher per-call overhead and interacts poorly with the SDPA fallback leading to memcpy+sync penalties. We'll roll a canary rebuild with FASTPATH_SMALL_SEQ enabled and add a selector telemetry patch.

aj-ml: please add an eval job to nightly perf bench to include seq_len 16/32/64 and batch sizes 1..8 so we catch similar regressions.

devon-runtime: done: I created perf task PERF-889 and scheduled runs.

beth-support: customer confirmed canary reduced p95 to ~130ms and p99 to ~260ms — they are happy to let us promote. :white_check_mark:

maria-engr: promotion steps: revert kernel policy on main to previous selector, and merge FASTPATH_SMALL_SEQ into build. I will open PR with diff and run CI.

devon-runtime: rolling the config to 25% now, watch dashboards.

kai-sre: alert cleared after 8m, p99 back to baseline. I'll close INC-4728 when promotion finishes.

beth-support: thanks team. please add a short postmortem with timeline, root cause, fix, and permanent mitigations (perf coverage + auto-fallback heuristics). I'll update ACME account notes. :thumbsup:

maria-engr: will do, drafting PM now.

devon-runtime: notes for postmortem: include repro script, commit abcd1234, canary hashes, and the kernel_selector telemetry patch id telem-102.

leo-compiler-bot: tagging logs for retention: `logs:retain:INC-4728 30d`.

beth-support: closing loop — customer to confirm after 24h, keeping on-watch. thanks everyone. :pray:
